title: Network Participation Agreements — Calculation of the Exit Settlement on an Ending DHMO Primary Care Agreement
content:
This calculation applies to a Cascade DHMO Primary Care Dentist Agreement under the **Network Participation Agreements** that is in termination pending status. It works out the exit settlement: the part of the agreement's open receivable that the capitation payments still due before the termination date are not expected to recover.

## Quantities

**Open receivable.** The total of the agreement's overpayment notices, less every withholding, refund and reduction booked against them, plus every claim payment remittance on the agreement. On a capitation agreement, each claim payment remittance repays an over-recovery.

**Capitation payments still due.** The whole months from today to the termination date, less one, and never below zero. One is deducted because assigned members are reassigned 30 days (the agreement type's reassignment lead time) before the termination date, and no capitation is paid for the month in which they leave.

**Payment amount.** Each capitation payment still due is taken at the amount of the agreement's most recent capitation payment.

**Exit recovery share.** The base exit recovery share, which is the agreement type's recoupment percentage from the product's payment integrity table. The exit recovery share is never below zero.

**Expected recovery.** The capitation payments still due, multiplied by the payment amount, multiplied by the exit recovery share and divided by one hundred. It is a single product, rounded once, at the end, half up to the cent.

**Exit settlement.** The open receivable less the expected recovery, rounded half up to the cent, and never below zero.

## Where it is recorded, and its ceiling

The exit settlement is recorded as a refund received against the overpayment under recovery. That is the overpayment the agreement's most recent withholding was applied to. The settlement is never more than that overpayment's open amount, which is its notice amount less every withholding, refund and reduction booked against it.

## When nothing is worked out

No exit settlement is worked out under this calculation when the agreement is not in termination pending status, is not paid by capitation, or has no capitation payment on record.

## Conventions

- Days are calendar days counted from the earlier date to the later date: the earlier date is not counted and the later date is.
- Whole months are the difference in calendar months, less one when the later date's day of the month is smaller than the earlier date's.
- Where two ledger entries or two panel requests a selection reads share the latest date or time, the one listed first on the agreement's records is taken.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

Today is 12 March and the termination date is 31 July. That is 4 whole months, so 3 capitation payments are still due. The most recent capitation payment is 7110.00 USD, and the recoupment percentage is 50 percent.

- Expected recovery: 3 times 7110.00 times 50, divided by one hundred, gives 10665.00 USD.
- Open receivable: notices of 15200.00 USD, less 4100.00 USD withheld, refunded or reduced, plus no claim payment remittances, gives 11100.00 USD.
- Exit settlement: 11100.00 less 10665.00 gives 435.00 USD.
- The overpayment under recovery has 2600.00 USD open, so the 435.00 USD stands.
